- Do request/response logs include full headers by default (Authorization, Cookie, X-Request-ID, etc.)? Can we mask or drop specific headers?

Hi Alice — great to meet you today. Quick recap and answers to your questions, plus next steps:

Recap / TL;DR:
- Redwood supports field-level and pattern-based redaction for request/response bodies and headers.
- We can drop or mask headers (Authorization, Cookie) by default via an allowlist/denylist on a per-route basis.
- Trace IDs: we support hashing/truncation or full strip before persisting logs; we can also provide a hashed mapping on request if you need internal correlation.
- PII detection: built-in detectors for emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit cards, and common personal identifiers. Detectors are configurable to reduce false positives.
- Retention: default hosted retention is 30 days, configurable up to 365 days for enterprise plans; Hosted US-only tenancy is supported. Private/VPC gives you full control over retention and storage.

Attachments I'm sharing now:
- SOC2-attestation.pdf (summary attestation)
- redaction-playbook.pdf (overview of redaction controls and recommended rules)

Proposed next steps:
1) Security call with our Product Security (Rachel) to walk through controls and your threat model — suggest Tue Feb 16 at 10:00 AM PT.
2) Share your specific retention/region requirement in this thread and we’ll confirm config options + quote for longer retention if needed.
3) If you want a demo of the redaction rules, we can provide a short sandbox and a sample logging-config.json for your infra to review.

If that works I’ll get Rachel added to the calendar invite and send over the sample config.

Hi — thanks, questions below with specifics and a few config examples. Rachel from Product Security is cc’d and will join the call.

Short answers:
- Header handling: configurable per-route via header_allowlist/header_denylist. Common sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Proxy-Authorization) are denylisted in our default profile and stripped prior to persistent logging. You can also choose to mask instead of drop.
- Trace IDs: we support three modes — preserve (raw), hash (SHA256 prefix), or strip. Hashing uses a salt unique to your tenancy so the mapping is not reversible. By default for hosted accounts we hash trace IDs; for Private deployments you can choose to preserve local trace ids behind your VPC.
- PII detection/redaction: in-process redaction happens at the inference node before logs are emitted. We use a combination of regex detectors and ML entity detectors. Rules are configurable and we can provide a sample rule-set to reduce false positives (e.g., exclude token-like strings of the model).
- Retention: hosted default is 30d. We can configure 90d or 365d on a commitment plan; for strict controls you can elect private hosting (Customer-managed S3) where you fully control retention and lifecycle policies.
- Data residency: Hosted US tenancy is available and will keep logs and telemetry in the US region. EU tenancy is available for EU-only customers. Private/VPC gives the strongest guarantee.

Sample config (excerpt):

"logging-config.json" (excerpt):
{
  "routes": [
    {
      "path": "/api/generate",
      "retain_headers": ["X-Request-ID", "X-Trace-Parent"],
      "drop_headers": ["Authorization", "Cookie", "Set-Cookie"],
      "body_redaction": ["email", "ssn", "credit_card"],
      "trace_id_mode": "hash",
      "hash_salt": "<customer-salt>"
    }
  ],
  "retention_days": 90
}

Operational notes:
- Redaction is applied in-process inside the inference runtime before logs are sent to our telemetry pipeline. We also apply an additional scrub in the aggregation layer as a secondary filter.
